questions.question: When and where did the first Asian Games take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951, New Delhi**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first Asian Games were held in **New Delhi, India** in **1951**. 
 
• This historic event marked the beginning of a significant multi-sport event for athletes from across the Asian continent.
 
• The inaugural Asian Games showcased a variety of sports and brought together athletes from different nations.
 
• It was a milestone in the history of Asian sports and laid the foundation for future Asian Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Asian Games were established to promote sportsmanship, friendship, and understanding among Asian nations.
 
• They are the second-largest multi-sport event in the world after the Olympic Games.
 
• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
 
• The Asian Games are held every four years, showcasing a wide range of sports disciplines.
 
• The Asian Games not only promote athletic competition but also serve as a platform for cultural exchange and understanding between different Asian nations.

questions.question: The UIDAI is under the jurisdiction of which of the following ministries?

options.text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The UIDAI (Unique Identification Authority of India) is under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
 
• The UIDAI is responsible for issuing Aadhaar cards, which are unique identification numbers assigned to Indian residents.
 
• It is a crucial government body that plays a significant role in various government services and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Ministry of Finance:**

 
 
• **​** This ministry primarily handles government finances, taxation, and economic policies.

 
 
• While UIDAI's operations involve financial transactions, its core function is related to digital identity, which is more closely aligned with technology and information technology.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Education:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for education policies and programs. UIDAI, though used in education-related activities, is not directly under its purview.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for internal security, law and order, and border security. While UIDAI can be used for identity verification in various security-related applications, its core function is not directly related to home affairs.

questions.question: Formulas in MS-Excel always start with which of the following symbols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** = **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Microsoft Excel, all formulas begin with an equal sign (=).
 
• This symbol tells Excel that the following characters constitute a formula, and it should perform the calculation or operation specified.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ! (Exclamation mark): Often used in Excel formulas for absolute cell references.

 
 
• For example, $A$1 indicates an absolute reference to cell A1, meaning that the reference won't change when the formula is copied to other cells.
 
 

 
• - (Minus sign): This is primarily used for subtraction operations within formulas.
 
 
• For instance, =A1-B1 subtracts the value in cell B1 from the value in cell A1.
 
 
 
• == (Double equal sign): This is not used to start formulas. It's a comparison operator used in logical expressions to check if two values are equal. For instance,
 
 
• =IF(A1=B1,"Equal","Not Equal") checks if the values in cells A1 and B1 are equal and returns "Equal" or "Not Equal" accordingly.

questions.question: The Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Sanga**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Khanua was fought between Babur and Rana Sanga**: 

 
 
• Babur: The founder of the Mughal Empire 
 
• Rana Sanga: The Rajput king of Mewar 
 
 
 
• The **battle took place on March 16, 152**7, near the village of Khanwa in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan.
 
• The **battle was a major event in Medieval Indian history** and was one of the earliest battles in Northern India to use gunpowder extensively. 
 
• **Babur won** the battle and became the predominant ruler of central and northern India.
 
• He t**ook the title of Ghazi after his victory.**
 
• The** defeat of Rana Sanga at Khanwa is considered a watershed moment in the Mughal conquest of Northern India. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rana Ratan Singh**

 
 
• Rana Ratan Singh is perhaps most famously known for his **association with the legendary queen Padmini**.
 
• The story of her beauty and sacrifice has been immortalized in the epic poem "Padmini".
 
• **His reign was marked by the siege of Chittor by the Delhi Sulta**n, Alauddin Khilji, who was captivated by the tales of Padmini's beauty.
 
• The **siege led to a heroic sacrifice by the Rajput warriors**, including Jauhar, a form of self-immolation by women to protect their honour.
 
 
 
• **Maharana Pratap**
 
 
• Maharana Pratap is **one of the most celebrated figures in Indian history**, known for his unwavering courage and resistance against the Mughal Empire.
 
• His** most famous battle was the Battle of Haldighati**, where he fought against the formidable Mughal forces led by Akbar.
 
• Though the battle resulted in a tactical defeat, it showcased the indomitable spirit of the Rajput warriors.
 
• He is **revered as a symbol of Rajput pride** and a fighter for freedom.

questions.question: Balasaraswati who was regarded as child prodigy by Vidhwans and Pandits played an important role in reviving the dance form ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Balasaraswati **was a famous Indian dancer and singer** who played an important role in reviving the **classical dance form Bharatanatyam**
 
• Balasaraswati **was a leading exponent of Bharatanatyam, a classical dance style that originated in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• She made this style of dancing well-known in India and around the world.
 
• Balasaraswati **received the Padma Bhushan in 1957, the Padma Vibhushan in 1977, and the Sangeetha Kalasikhamani Award in 1981.**
 
• Balasaraswati **was the only non-western dancer included in the 2000 compilation,**
 
 
• The Irreplaceable Treasures of Dance in America: The First 100. Bengali film director Satyajit Ray made a documentary film on Balasaraswati called Bala in 1976
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is the oldest and major classical dance form of India that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatanatyam is a solo dance performed only by women.
 
• According to the Hindu tradition the name of the dance form was derived by joining two words, ‘Bharata’ and Natyam’ where ‘Natyam in Sanskrit means dance and ‘Bharata’ is a mnemonic comprising ‘bha’, ‘ra’ and ‘ta’ which respectively means ‘bhava’ that is emotion and feelings; ‘raga’ that is a melody; and ‘tala’ that is rhythm.
 
• ‘Natya Shastra’ is the ancient Sanskrit Hindu text on the performing arts, the theoretical base of this form traces back.
 
• Bharatanatyam performance consists of six portions: Alarippu, Jathiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam and Tillana
 
 
 
• **Kathak**:
 
 
• Kathak is a classical dance form that originated in Northern India of Uttar Pradesh referred to as Kathakars or storytellers for portraying the epic tales from Hindu scriptures, Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
• The Kathakars communicate stories through rhythmic foot movements, hand gestures, facial expressions, and eye work.
 
• This performing art that incorporates legends from ancient mythology and great Indian epics, especially from the life of Lord Krishna became quite popular in the courts of North Indian kingdoms.
 
• Three specific forms of this genre that is three Gharanas (schools), which mostly differ in the emphasis given to footwork versus acting, are more famous names, the Jaipur Gharana, the Benaras Gharana, and the Lucknow Gharana.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**:
 
 
• Mohiniyattam is a major classical dance form of India that originated in Kerala.
 
• Mohiniattam derives its name from the word ‘Mohini’, a female avatar of Lord Vishnu. 
 
• Mohiniattam adheres to the Lasya type that showcases a more graceful, gentle, and feminine form of dancing.
 
• Mohiniyattam is a solo dance performed only by female artists, it emotes a play through dancing and singing where the song is customarily in Manipravala which is a mix of Sanskrit and Malayalam language and the recitation may be either performed by the dancer herself or by a vocalist with the music style being Carnatic.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a major classical dance form of India that originated in a village of the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Kuchipudi is a religious art rooting back to the age-old Hindu Sanskrit text ‘Natya Shastra’ and connects traditionally with temples, spiritual faiths and traveling bards.
 
• This ancient dance form finds a place in the 10th-century copper inscriptions and in 15th-century texts like ‘Machupalli Kaifat’.
 
• Traditionally it is regarded that the sannyasin of Advaita Vedanta sect, Tirtha Narayana Yati, and his disciple Siddhendra Yogi initiated, methodized and arranged the present day version of the dance form in the 17th century.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I- Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.

II- All India Radio came into being in 1936.

III - In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Door darshan (DD).

options.text: Both I and II are correct.
I, II and III are correct
Both II and III are correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** I, II and III are correct**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the Radio Club of Bombay.**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• The first radio broadcast in India was made by the Radio Club of Bombay in 1923.
 
 
 
• **II. All India Radio came into being in 1936.**
 
 
• This statement is also **correct**.
 
• All India Radio (AIR) was formed in 1936, taking over the operations of the Indian State Broadcasting Service.
 
 
 
• **III. In 1976, TV was delinked from All India Radio (AIR) and got a separate identity as Doordarshan (DD).**
 
 
• This statement is **correct** as well.
 
• In 1976, television broadcasting was separated from All India Radio and established as an independent entity, Doordarshan.
 
 
 
• Therefore, all three statements are accurate

questions.question: El Nino is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in which ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Pacific Ocean**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• El Niño is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in the **eastern tropical Pacific Ocean**. 
 
• This warming event has significant impacts on weather patterns around the globe, affecting rainfall, temperature, and wind patterns.
 
• During an El Niño event, the trade winds, which typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean, weaken or reverse direction.
 
• This allows warm water to accumulate in the eastern Pacific, leading to changes in atmospheric pressure and circulation.
 
• The impacts of El Niño can be far-reaching, affecting weather patterns in regions as diverse as South America, Africa, and Southeast Asia.
 
• Some of the potential impacts of El Niño include:
 
 
• Increased rainfall: In some regions, such as the southern United States and parts of South America, El Niño can lead to increased rainfall and flooding.
 
• Drought: In other regions, such as Australia and Southeast Asia, El Niño can cause drought and reduced rainfall.
 
• Changes in ocean ecosystems: Warmer water temperatures can disrupt marine ecosystems, affecting fish populations and coral reefs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Arctic Ocean:**

 
 
• This is the smallest of the world's five oceans, located in the Northern Hemisphere. 
 
 
 
• **Indian Ocean:**
 
 
• This ocean is located between Africa, Asia, and Australia. 
 
 
 
• **Atlantic Ocean:**
 
 
• This ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of concurrent list from ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Australia**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Constitution**, while unique in many respects, **drew** inspiration from **various sources, including the Australian Constitution.**
 
• One significant** borrowing is the concept of the Concurrent List.**
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
 
• This** list outlines subjects on which both the central government and state governments have the power to legislate**.
 
• This arrangement is designed to balance the powers of the central and state governments, ensuring a harmonious federal structure.
 
 
 
• Some of the **subjects included in the Concurrent List are**:
 
 
• Education
 
• Forests
 
• Wildlife protection
 
• Marriage and divorce
 
• Criminal law and procedure
 
 
 
• If both the central and state governments enact laws on a concurrent subject, **the central law prevails**.
 
• However, i**n case of inconsistency, the state law can be overridden by a central law.**
 
• By incorporating the Concurrent List, t**he Indian Constitution aims to achieve a balance between national unity and state autonomy, **enabling both levels of government to address issues of national and regional importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The other borrowed provisions from different countries and details of those are given in below:

questions.question: Which of these is NOT true of the second phase of the green revolution?

options.text: It was launched in areas with a significant shift from dry to wet (irrigated) cultivation.
It covered the period of the 1980s.
It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s.
It was adopted by farmers living in dry and semi-arid regions of India.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The second phase of the Green Revolution, which occurred in the 1980s,
 
 
• aimed to expand the benefits of the Green Revolution to areas with less favourable conditions, such as dry and semi-arid regions.
 
 
 
• **First Phase (1960s-1970s):**
 
 
• Focused on introducing high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds and chemical fertilizers to increase agricultural production.
 
• Primarily targeted areas with adequate irrigation facilities, such as the Punjab and Haryana regions.
 
 
 
• **Second Phase (1980s):**
 
 
• Expanded the Green Revolution to areas with less favorable conditions, including dry and semi-arid regions.
 
• Introduced drought-resistant and early-maturing crop varieties.
 
• Promoted integrated pest management and soil conservation practices.
 
• Emphasized the need for sustainable agriculture to reduce environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Therefore, the statement "It covered the period of the 1960s and 1970s" is incorrect.**
 
 
• The second phase of the Green Revolution took place in the 1980s, building upon the successes of the first phase and aiming to further enhance agricultural productivity and food security in India.

questions.question: In which year did a trio of scientists, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, prove that except viruses, all living organisms have DNA as their genetic material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1944**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1944, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty conducted experiments that demonstrated that DNA is the substance that causes bacterial transformation.
 
• Their findings provided critical evidence that DNA is the hereditary material in organisms, excluding viruses, which can have RNA as their genetic material.
 
• This was one of the first significant steps in molecular biology that led to the identification of DNA as the carrier of genetic information.
 
• Their work built upon Frederick Griffith's experiment in 1928, which suggested the existence of a "transforming principle" that could transfer genetic information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**

 
 
• DNA is a molecule that carries most of the genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• DNA is composed of two strands that coil around each other to form a double helix, carrying the genetic instructions in sequences of four types of nucleotides: adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
 
 
• **RNA (Ribonucleic Acid)**
 
 
• RNA is a molecule essential in various biological roles in coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes.
 
• RNA is usually single-stranded and is composed of nucleotides: adenine (A), uracil (U), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
• In some viruses, RNA acts as the genetic material instead of DNA.
 
 
 
• **Bacterial Transformation**
 
 
• Bacterial transformation is a process by which bacterial cells take up foreign DNA molecules and incorporate them into their own genetic material, leading to genetic changes.
 
• This process was first observed by Frederick Griffith in 1928, which led to the discovery of the "transforming principle" later identified as DNA by Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty.
 
 
 
• **Griffith's Experiment**
 
 
• Griffith's experiment demonstrated that a substance from dead bacteria could genetically transform living bacteria.
 
• He worked with two strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae: a virulent S strain with a smooth capsule and a non-virulent R strain without a capsule.
 
• His results showed that heat-killed S strain bacteria could transfer genetic material to the R strain, making it virulent.

questions.question: Where was the first Durand Cup, India’s oldest football tournament, held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shimla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Durand Cup is the oldest football tournament in India and was first held in 1888.
 
• The tournament was named after Mortimer Durand, who was the Foreign Secretary in charge of India at that time.
 
• The inaugural tournament was held in Shimla, which served as the summer capital of British India.
 
• Initially, the tournament was started as a football competition for British troops stationed in India but later it was opened to civilians as well.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Durand Cup**

 
 
• The Durand Cup is named after Sir Mortimer Durand, who was the Foreign Secretary of British India from 1884 to 1894.
 
• It is one of the oldest football competitions in the world and the oldest in Asia.
 
• The tournament is organized annually and has seen participation from top football clubs in India.
 
• Winners of the Durand Cup are awarded three trophies: the President's Cup (added in 1956), the Durand Cup (the original trophy), and the Shimla Trophy (added in 1904).
 
 
 
• **Football in India**
 
 
• Football is one of the most popular sports in India, especially in states like West Bengal, Goa, Kerala, and the northeastern states.
 
• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) is the governing body for football in India.
 
• The Indian Super League (ISL) and I-League are the top professional football leagues in the country.
 
• India has a rich history in football, with clubs like Mohun Bagan and East Bengal having a storied legacy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate is incorrect as of 31 March 2024?

options.text: The scheme was announced in the 2023-24 budget.
The maximum limit of deposit in the scheme is 2 lakhs per year.
The tenure of the scheme is 5 years.
The scheme is validup to 31 March 2025.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate scheme was announced in the 2023-24 budget.
 
• The maximum limit of deposit in the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate scheme is 2 lakhs per year.
 
• The tenure of the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate scheme is 2 years, not 5 years.
 
• The Mahila Samman Savings Certificate scheme is valid up to 31 March 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahila Samman Savings Certificate Scheme:**

 
 
• This scheme aims to empower women by encouraging savings and providing a secure investment option.
 
• The scheme offers attractive interest rates to encourage more women to participate in formal financial systems.
 
• The minimum deposit amount is ₹1,000, and the maximum is ₹2,00,000 per financial year.
 
• The interest rate for the scheme is determined by the government and is revised periodically.
 
 
 
• **Budget 2023-24:**
 
 
• Presented by the Finance Minister, this budget included various schemes and allocations for different sectors.
 
• The budget focused on infrastructure development, healthcare, education, and social welfare.
 
• Special emphasis was placed on empowering women, youth, and economically weaker sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Savings Certificates:**
 
 
• Savings certificates are government-backed investment instruments that offer fixed returns over a specified period.
 
• They are considered a safe investment option as they are backed by the government and provide guaranteed returns.
 
• Examples include National Savings Certificates (NSC) and Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP).

questions.question: Who proposed that ‘Light is made up of waves propagating perpendicular to the direction of its movement’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Huygens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Christiaan Huygens** was a Dutch physicist, mathematician, astronomer and inventor.
 
• He is best known for his wave theory of light, which he described in his book **"Traité de la Lumière"** (Treatise on Light) in 1690.
 
• Huygens proposed that **light is made up of waves** that propagate perpendicular to the direction of its movement.
 
• This wave theory of light was later supported by the experiments of **Thomas Young** and **Augustin-Jean Fresnel**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wave Theory of Light:**

 
 
• The wave theory of light suggests that light travels in the form of waves.
 
• According to Huygens' principle, every point on a wavefront is a source of wavelets that spread out in the forward direction at the same speed as the wave itself.
 
• The new wavefront is the tangent to all of these secondary wavelets.
 
• This theory was instrumental in explaining phenomena such as interference and diffraction, which could not be explained by the particle theory of light.
 
 
 
• **Particle Theory of Light:**
 
 
• The particle theory of light, proposed by Isaac Newton, suggested that light is made up of particles called corpuscles.
 
• This theory was successful in explaining the reflection and refraction of light but failed to explain interference and diffraction.
 
 
 
• **Thomas Young's Double-Slit Experiment:**
 
 
• Thomas Young's double-slit experiment demonstrated the wave nature of light.
 
• When light passes through two closely spaced slits, it creates an interference pattern on a screen behind the slits.
 
• This pattern of bright and dark fringes can only be explained if light behaves as a wave.
 
 
 
• **Augustin-Jean Fresnel:**
 
 
• Fresnel made significant contributions to the wave theory of light.
 
• He developed the Fresnel equations, which describe how light behaves at the interface between two different media.
 
• Fresnel's work on diffraction and interference further confirmed the wave nature of light.

questions.question: In the Hindustani music system, the ________ are allotted to different hours of the day and different seasons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ragas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Hindustani music system, ragas are specifically designed to be played or sung during certain times of the day or seasons.
 
• Each raga has a distinct mood and is intended to invoke specific emotions, often linked with the time of day or season it is associated with.
 
• The practice of associating ragas with different times of the day or seasons helps in enhancing the emotional and aesthetic experience of the listener.
 
• This tradition has been an integral part of Indian classical music, helping to preserve its rich heritage and cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ragas**

 
 
• A raga is a melodic framework for improvisation akin to a melodic mode in Indian classical music.
 
• It is a set of rules for building a melody – the specific notes that can be used and the motifs that can be played.
 
• Ragas are meant to express certain emotions and are associated with different times of the day or seasons.
 
• There are hundreds of ragas, each with its own unique characteristics and mood.
 
 
 
• **Varnas**
 
 
• In the context of music, varnas refer to the patterns of notes in classical compositions.
 
• These are used to teach and practice the various aspects of a raga.
 
• The term "varna" is also used in a different context in Indian culture, referring to the classification of society.
 
 
 
• **Gita**
 
 
• The term "gita" typically refers to a song or a hymn.
 
• In the context of Indian classical music, it can refer to compositions that are sung.
 
• The most famous "Gita" in Indian culture is the Bhagavad Gita, a 700-verse Hindu scripture that is part of the Indian epic Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Srutis**
 
 
• Srutis are the microtones or the smallest intervals of pitch that the human ear can detect.
 
• They are fundamental to the tuning system in Indian classical music.
 
• There are 22 srutis in an octave in Indian classical music, providing a finer division of pitch compared to the Western music system.

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork, along with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical dance form from Kerala, characterized by graceful, swaying body movements and subtle facial expressions, typically performed by women.
 
• **Garba** is a popular folk dance from Gujarat, performed in a circle, with rhythmic clapping and twirling, usually during the Navratri festival.
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form from Assam, originally performed by male monks in the monasteries as part of their religious rituals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**

 
 
• It is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India.
 
• Originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu, it was traditionally performed by devadasis.
 
• It is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and knees flexed out, combined with spectacular footwork.
 
• It involves intricate hand gestures (mudras) and facial expressions to convey different emotions.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam**
 
 
• This dance form is named after Mohini, the female avatar of Vishnu.
 
• It combines elements of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, another classical dance from Kerala.
 
• Known for its graceful movements and gentle swaying, it is often performed solo by women.
 
 
 
• **Garba**
 
 
• It is traditionally performed during the Navratri festival in Gujarat.
 
• Garba is danced in a circle around an idol or picture of the Goddess Durga.
 
• It is characterized by rhythmic clapping, twirling, and coordinated movements.
 
• Garba is a community dance where everyone participates, reflecting the social and cultural harmony.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**
 
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev in Assam.
 
• Originally performed in monasteries (sattras) by male monks, it has now gained popularity among female dancers as well.
 
• Sattriya incorporates various elements of drama, dance, and music and is performed as part of religious rituals.

questions.question: Which organisation was started in the Pune district of Maharashtra in 1873 with the aim of promoting education and social rights among the underprivileged group of society?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyashodhak Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra in 1873.
 
• The organization aimed at social reforms including the upliftment of the underprivileged sections of society, especially the lower castes.
 
• It promoted the values of human rights, equality, and education among the oppressed communities.
 
• The organization also focused on eradicating social evils like untouchability and promoting women's rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotirao Phule**

 
 
• Jyotirao Phule was a prominent social reformer and activist in Maharashtra, India.
 
• He is best known for his efforts to promote education for women and lower castes, and his work against the caste system.
 
• Phule, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, opened the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• He wrote several books and plays that criticized the caste system and called for social equality.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms in India**
 
 
• Social reforms in India have historically focused on eradicating social evils like sati, child marriage, untouchability, and promoting education and women's rights.
 
• Various social reform movements were led by individuals like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Jyotirao Phule, and B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• These movements played a crucial role in shaping modern Indian society and its values of equality and justice.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Education**
 
 
• Education is a powerful tool for social change and empowerment.
 
• It helps in the development of critical thinking, self-reliance, and the ability to participate fully in society.
 
• Promoting education among the underprivileged sections of society can help in breaking the cycle of poverty and social inequality.
 
 
 
• **Women's Rights**
 
 
• Women's rights are fundamental to achieving gender equality and empowering women to make decisions about their lives.
 
• Promoting women's education, health, and economic participation can lead to more inclusive and sustainable development.
 
• Social reform movements have historically emphasized the importance of women's rights as a key component of social progress.

questions.question: In which year was Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA) was **introduced in 2015**.
 
• It was launched by the Prime Minister of India, **Narendra Modi**, on **8th April 2015**.
 
• MUDRA aims to provide **funding to the non-corporate, non-farm sector income-generating activities** of micro and small enterprises whose credit needs are below ₹10 lakh.
 
• The initiative is part of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) which aims to **‘fund the unfunded’** through various financial institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA)**

 
 
• MUDRA was set up through a statutory enactment and is responsible for developing and refinancing all Micro-finance Institutions which are in the business of lending to micro/small business entities.
 
• It provides refinance support to banks, Microfinance Institutions (MFIs), and other eligible institutions which are in the business of lending to micro/small business entities engaged in manufacturing, trading, and service activities.
 
• The primary objective of MUDRA is to create an inclusive, sustainable, and value-based entrepreneurial culture, in collaboration with partner institutions in delivering comprehensive financial support to the bottom of the pyramid universe.
 
• MUDRA offers three types of loans: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)**
 
 
• It is a scheme launched by the Government of India to provide loans up to ₹10 lakh to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro-enterprises.
 
• These loans are classified as MUDRA loans under PMMY.
 
• The loans are given by Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.
 
• The aim is to promote entrepreneurship among the younger generation, women, and marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of MUDRA Scheme**
 
 
• MUDRA aims to fund the unfunded by bringing such enterprises to the formal financial system and extending affordable credit to them.
 
• It helps in creating job opportunities and encouraging self-employment.
 
• The scheme also aims to provide a credit guarantee to these small businesses to ensure their sustainability and growth.
 
• It plays a crucial role in boosting the Indian economy by promoting the micro-enterprise sector.

questions.question: Which shortcut key is used to paste a slide in Microsoft PowerPoint?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CTRL + V**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **CTRL + V** is the standard keyboard shortcut used to paste the copied content in most applications including Microsoft PowerPoint.
 
• This shortcut allows users to quickly paste slides, text, or other objects that have been copied to the clipboard.
 
• Using keyboard shortcuts like **CTRL + V** can significantly enhance productivity by reducing the time taken to navigate through menus.
 
• This command works consistently across various Microsoft Office applications such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CTRL + C**

 
 
• This is the shortcut key used to copy the selected content to the clipboard.
 
• It does not remove the original content from the source location.
 
 
 
• **CTRL + X**
 
 
• This shortcut key is used to cut the selected content, which removes it from the source location and copies it to the clipboard.
 
 
 
• **CTRL + P**
 
 
• This shortcut key is used to open the Print dialog box in most applications, allowing users to print the current document or slide.
 
 
 
• **Clipboard**
 
 
• The clipboard is a temporary storage area for data that the user wants to copy from one place to another.
 
• It holds the data until the user decides to paste it elsewhere or until the system is shut down.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey 2022-23, the Labour Force Participation Rate for males has gone up to ________in 2020-21.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.575**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) is an important metric that indicates the percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• According to the Economic Survey 2022-23, the LFPR for males in India increased to 0.575 (57.5%) in the year 2020-21.
 
• This increase suggests a positive trend in male participation in the labor market during that period.
 
• The LFPR is a critical indicator for assessing the economic activity level and the potential labor supply within a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**

 
 
• The LFPR is defined as the percentage of the working-age population (usually ages 15-64) that is part of the labor force. The labor force includes both the employed and the unemployed who are actively looking for work.
 
• A higher LFPR indicates a higher proportion of the working-age population that is participating in the labor market, either by working or seeking work.
 
• The LFPR is an important indicator for policymakers to understand the availability of labor in the economy and to make informed decisions regarding employment policies and programs.
 
• The LFPR can be influenced by various factors, including economic conditions, social and cultural norms, education levels, and government policies.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey**
 
 
• The Economic Survey is an annual document released by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, which reviews the developments in the Indian economy over the past financial year.
 
• It provides an overview of the economic performance, identifies key challenges, and outlines the prospects for the coming year.
 
• The Economic Survey is an important tool for policymakers, economists, and researchers to understand the current state of the economy and to formulate policies for sustainable growth and development.
 
• It covers various aspects of the economy, including GDP growth, inflation, employment, trade, fiscal policy, and sectoral performance.
 
 
 
• **Employment and Unemployment**
 
 
• Employment refers to the situation where individuals are engaged in productive activities and receive compensation for their work.
 
• Unemployment refers to the situation where individuals who are capable of working and are actively seeking work are unable to find employment.
 
• The unemployment rate is a key indicator of labor market conditions and is calculated as the percentage of the labor force that is unemployed.
 
• Reducing unemployment and increasing employment opportunities are important goals for governments to ensure economic stability and improve the standard of living for their citizens.

questions.question: Any citizen of India can make a declaration renouncing his/her Indian citizenship under the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citizenship Act, 1955**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** is the primary legislation governing the acquisition and loss of Indian citizenship.
 
• Under this Act, any Indian citizen can renounce their Indian citizenship by making a declaration.
 
• The renunciation of citizenship is a formal process detailed in the Act and ensures that the individual is no longer considered an Indian citizen.
 
• The Act also covers other aspects of citizenship such as acquisition, termination, and registration of citizenship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955**

 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955, provides the basis for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• It specifies five modes of acquiring citizenship: by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• The Act outlines the processes and criteria for each mode, ensuring clear guidelines for obtaining Indian citizenship.
 
• Amendments to the Act have been made over the years to address various aspects of citizenship and to update the legal framework in line with changing needs and circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Renunciation of Citizenship**
 
 
• Renunciation of citizenship is a voluntary act where an individual formally declares their intention to give up Indian citizenship.
 
• This process is essential for individuals who wish to acquire citizenship of another country that does not allow dual citizenship.
 
• The declaration must be made in the prescribed manner, and upon its acceptance, the individual ceases to be an Indian citizen.
 
• Renunciation also extends to any minor children of the individual, but they have the right to resume Indian citizenship upon reaching adulthood.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)**
 
 
• The OCI scheme provides a form of residency status to persons of Indian origin who are citizens of other countries, allowing them to live and work in India indefinitely.
 
• OCI cardholders do not have the right to vote, hold constitutional office, or buy agricultural land, but they enjoy many of the same rights as Indian citizens.
 
• This scheme facilitates easier travel to and from India and allows for long-term residency without the need for repeated visa applications.

questions.question:
With reference to Chethiagiri Vihar festival consider the following statements and select the correct option.

i) It is a Buddhist festival.

ii) It is held at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh.

iii) Relics of SariPutta and Maha Moggallana are worshiped.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chethiagiri Vihar festival is indeed a **Buddhist festival**.
 
• The festival is held at **Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• During the festival, **relics of Sariputta and Maha Moggallana** are worshipped.
 
• This festival is an important event for Buddhists, attracting many pilgrims to Sanchi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanchi:**

 
 
• Sanchi is a small village in the Raisen District of the state of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It is famous for its Buddhist stupas, especially the Great Stupa which is one of the oldest stone structures in India.
 
• Sanchi was a major Buddhist center in India, dating back to the 3rd century BCE, commissioned by Emperor Ashoka.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism:**
 
 
• Buddhism is a religion and philosophy that developed from the teachings of the Buddha (Sanskrit: "Awakened One"), a teacher who lived in northern India between the mid-6th and mid-4th centuries BCE.
 
• Buddhism spread throughout Asia and is now a global religion.
 
• The core beliefs include the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
 
 
 
• **Sariputta and Maha Moggallana:**
 
 
• Sariputta and Maha Moggallana were two of the most important disciples of the Buddha.
 
• They are often depicted as the Buddha's chief attendants and are revered for their great wisdom and spiritual powers.
 
• Their relics are considered sacred and are venerated by Buddhists around the world.
